texts: mixed: the deciding event, the Council as its agent and consensus as the method all land correctly. The one bad atom is the record of the word "usually": it names this particular Council where the translator's format requires a kind, because a frequency adverb attached to a single named body has no licensed slot, so the "usually" is stored in a shape nothing downstream can match. Rewrite as "The Council decides most matters by consensus." — "most matters" gives the frequency an honest range the translator can record (swap "matters" for whatever the Council actually decides).

mixed: the "when consensus fails" half is right and produces a rule that can actually fire, giving a vote whenever consensus fails. But "a show of hands" was frozen into one opaque symbol with no internal parts, so nothing in the parse connects it to hands or to showing them and a question about how the vote is taken hits a dead end. Rewrite as "When consensus fails, the Council votes by raised hands." so the hands are ordinary things the parse can reach.

bad: the sentence states a standing procedure, but an indefinite singular subject ("a simple majority") forces the translator to read it as one particular majority settling one particular vote, so nothing in the parse applies to any other vote. Two smaller distortions ride along: "simple" is asserted as a passing description of that majority rather than being kept as part of the named threshold "simple majority", and the vote is filed under the role for objects the deciding physically alters. Rewrite as "Every vote is decided by a simple majority." — the explicit "every" forces a genuine rule that covers all votes, not one occasion.
good. the speaker, the breaking and the tied vote are all covered, and the unmarked present tense correctly reads as the standing practice rather than as a single past occasion.
good. rarity is recorded as a property of ties as a kind, which is what the sentence says — it does not wrongly claim of any individual tie that it is rare.
